evidence: The frozen workbook row 28 (Quality Checks!A29:D29; matching Internal row 29) requires independent, noncontradictory criteria. Current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md explicitly gives independent credit priority over whole-flow grouping. Its S37 procedure at tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:467 separately reads the dirty editor and saved head but maps both results to this one row. Public environment/instructions/behaviour.md:34 promises both protections. These after-action preservation results are independently useful promises, not merely shared setup. Other reviewed ownership boundaries are explicit: cancellation/rollback/recovery, stale server refusal/draft/reapply, and current/history/retry restart outcomes. counterexample: A read-only history view that never writes the saved head but overwrites the unsaved editor with current saved fields on close satisfies persisted-state safety and loses the entire row. Conversely, a dialog can preserve the exact dirty buffer while mistakenly restoring the inspected snapshot on the server; its valid draft preservation also earns no independent credit. Both are plausible partial apps, not whole-product conforming apps. A conforming dialog/side-panel implementation with an independent retained dirty buffer is permitted; no conflicting product requirement was found.
suggested_fix: Keep the same S37 inspection scenario and split unchanged-current-record and retained-dirty-draft observations into separate binary outcomes with the existing combined 0.6 weight, without inheriting either result from the other.
